title: Low-degree evaluation and functorial construction for continuous procyclic cochains
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and let $F$ be a normed field with an isometric field embedding $\mathbf Q_\ell\hookrightarrow F$. Completeness of $F$ is not assumed. On the coherent site of profinite sets in [def-weil-size-convention], with finite jointly surjective covering families, put $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For $q\geq0$ set $U_F^q(S)=C(S\times H^q,F)$ with $A_F(S)$ acting through $S$, and set $U_F^q=0$ for $q<0$. Set $d^0=0$ and, for $q\geq1$, define
$$(df)(s;t_1,\ldots,t_{q+1})=f(s;t_2,\ldots,t_{q+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{q}(-1)^if(s;t_1,\ldots,t_i+t_{i+1},\ldots,t_{q+1})+(-1)^{q+1}f(s;t_1,\ldots,t_q).$$
These are sheaves of internal $A_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and these differentials satisfy $d^{q+1}d^q=0$. Put $K_F^0=K_F^1=A_F$, zero in other degrees, with zero differential. The formulas $\epsilon^0=1$, $\epsilon^1(f)(s)=f(s;1)$ and $\epsilon^q=0$ for $q\geq2$ define a morphism of these sheaf complexes. The maps $\epsilon$ commute with restriction under every continuous map of profinite parameter sets, including the empty set, and with postcomposition by every continuous field embedding over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. For every profinite $S$, evaluation at $1$ gives an $A_F(S)$-linear bijection
$$\{f\in C(S\times H,F): f(s;x+y)=f(s;x)+f(s;y)\}\xrightarrow{\sim} C(S,F),$$
whose inverse sends $a$ to $((s,t)\mapsto t a(s))$. Consequently $H^0(U_F(S))\to H^0(K_F(S))$ and $H^1(U_F(S))\to H^1(K_F(S))$ are isomorphisms of abstract modules, with no closure of boundaries.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-formulated scalar analytic input, extracted from Returned scalar-cochain proof steps 1–3: face cancellation, sheaf descent, evaluation naturality and dense-integer low-degree calculation. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) supplies only the cochain differential, not this theorem.

proof.text: The ring sheaf $A_F$ is supplied by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite jointly surjective cover $(S_i\to S)$, let $T=\coprod_i S_i$. A matching family $f_i\in C(S_i\times H^q,F)$ gives a continuous function on $T\times H^q$, constant on the fibres of $p:T\times H^q\to S\times H^q$: matching on $S_i\times_S S_j$ is exactly equality of those values. Applied with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, so $\mathcal O_E=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $A_n=\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell$, [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] (1)--(2) says that $H$ with its inverse-limit topology is homeomorphic to $\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its norm topology and is compact Hausdorff. Hence $T\times H^q$ is compact, as a finite product of compact spaces, $S\times H^q$ is Hausdorff, and $p$ is continuous and surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] with the whole spaces as its subsets. The resulting set function $f:S\times H^q\to F$ is continuous, since for every open $O\subseteq F$ the inverse image $p^{-1}(f^{-1}(O))$ is open and $p$ is quotient. Surjectivity proves uniqueness. For $S=\varnothing$ there is exactly one function, the zero module, so also the empty covering satisfies descent. Thus every $U_F^q$ is an abelian sheaf, with the zero sheaf in negative degrees.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: continuous-function descent on products

proof.text: For each $S$, $(a\cdot f)(s;\mathbf t)=a(s)f(s;\mathbf t)$ is continuous and additive in each argument. It commutes with restrictions. By the sheafified objectwise tensor description in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], these bilinear maps induce $A_F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}U_F^q\to U_F^q$. Associativity and the unit equation are the pointwise identities $(ab)f=a(bf)$ and $1f=f$, so they give precisely the module action of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Every face map leaves $s$ fixed and is continuous: it drops the first or last $H$ coordinate or replaces two adjacent coordinates by their sum. Pullback along it is $A_F(S)$-linear; a finite signed sum is continuous and linear. Hence the displayed $d^q$, including $d^0=0$, are morphisms of internal $A_F$-modules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: internal module structures and linear continuous differentials

proof.text: Write $b_i^n:H^{n+1}\to H^n$ for the face dropping the first coordinate ($i=0$), adding coordinates $i,i+1$ ($1\le i\le n$), or dropping the last ($i=n+1$). For $0\le i<j\le n+2$, $b_i^n b_j^{n+1}=b_{j-1}^n b_i^{n+1}$. If the operations involve disjoint coordinates this just says that performing them in either order gives the same ordered list. For adjacent merges it says $(x+y)+z=x+(y+z)$; if a dropping operation meets a merge, both sides delete the same initial or final two coordinates. This includes the two end drops. In $d^{n+1}d^n f$ pair the term $f\circ b_i^n\circ b_j^{n+1}$ with indices $(i,j)$, $i<j$, with the term having indices $(j-1,i)$. These pairs exhaust the double sum, since the complementary region is $i\ge j$. Their signs are $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{j-1+i}$, so they cancel. This proves $d^{n+1}d^n=0$ for $n\ge1$. At $n=0$ the composite vanishes because $d^0=0$, and negative degrees are zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: explicit face-pair cancellation; Stacks 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, differential formula

proof.text: Evaluation along the continuous map $s\mapsto(s,1)$ sends $U_F^1(S)$ to $A_F(S)$ and is $A_F(S)$-linear. It commutes with restriction, and $\epsilon^0$ is the identity while the other components are zero. The only potentially nonzero chain-map condition is $\epsilon^1d^0=d_K^0\epsilon^0$, whose two sides are zero. For the next condition both $\epsilon^2$ and $d_K^1$ are zero; all remaining conditions also have zero target. Thus $\epsilon$ is a morphism of the internal-module complexes constructed above.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: evaluation is a chain map

proof.text: For $u:S'\to S$, both composites in the degree-one naturality square send $f$ to $s'\mapsto f(u(s');1)$; in degree zero both are restriction, and elsewhere both are zero. If $j:F\hookrightarrow F'$ is a continuous field embedding over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, both coefficient composites send $f$ to $s\mapsto j(f(s;1))$. Postcomposition preserves the differential because $j$ preserves addition, negation and finite sums, and preserves actions after scalar change because $j(af)=j(a)j(f)$. These formulas prove every asserted compatibility, including $S'=\varnothing$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: parameter and coefficient naturality with explicit formulas

proof.text: For an additive $f\in C(S\times H,F)$ put $a(s)=f(s;1)$; it is continuous by restriction. For fixed $s$, additivity gives $f(s;0)=0$ and induction gives $f(s;n)=n a(s)$ for all $n\ge0$. For $t\in H$ choose the representative $n_m\in\{0,\ldots,\ell^m-1\}$ of its residue modulo $\ell^m$. In the inverse-limit topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $n_m\to t$: each residue modulo $\ell^k$ agrees with that of $t$ for $m\ge k$. Continuity of $f(s;-)$ gives $f(s;n_m)\to f(s;t)$; continuity of the inclusion $H\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\hookrightarrow F$ (the inverse-limit topology of $H$ is the norm topology by [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] (1) with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the embedding is isometric) and of multiplication gives $n_m a(s)\to t a(s)$. The two sequences coincide, so uniqueness of a limit in the Hausdorff normed field $F$ gives $f(s;t)=t a(s)$. This constructs no limit in $F$; both limits are already supplied by the indicated continuous maps, so completeness is unnecessary.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: residue representatives and the low-degree uniqueness argument

proof.text: Conversely, for $a\in C(S,F)$ the map $g_a(s,t)=t a(s)$ is jointly continuous, since $H\to\mathbf Q_\ell$ is continuous for the inverse-limit topology by [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] (1) with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, the field embedding is isometric and hence continuous and multiplication in $F$ is continuous. Distributivity gives $g_a(s,x+y)=g_a(s,x)+g_a(s,y)$, and $g_a(s,1)=a(s)$. The preceding step gives $g_{\epsilon^1(f)}=f$. Evaluation is $A_F(S)$-linear, and $g_{ba}(s,t)=t b(s)a(s)=b(s)g_a(s,t)$, so its inverse is also linear. This proves the asserted linear bijection for every $S$, including the empty set, where both modules have one element.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-supplied scalar analytic input: continuous explicit inverse and scalar linearity

proof.text: In degree zero, $U_F^0(S)=A_F(S)$ and both its incoming differential and $d^0$ are zero, so $H^0(U_F(S))=A_F(S)$ and $H^0(\epsilon)$ is the identity. In degree one the displayed formula is $d^1f(s;x,y)=f(s;y)-f(s;x+y)+f(s;x)$, so its kernel is exactly the additive families of steps 6--7. Its incoming image is zero because $d^0=0$. The target $K_F(S)$ has zero differentials, so $H^1(K_F(S))=A_F(S)$ and its induced map is exactly the bijection just proved. These are ordinary kernel/image quotients of abstract modules; no topological closure is taken.
